question:
Analise o(s) documento(s) de cenário do projeto e gere o SRS completo no formato especificado, seguindo o processo de trabalho: buscas dedicadas na base de conhecimento para cada tipo de artefato, rastreabilidade validada entre os artefatos.

Documento(s) de cenário:
--- Project Scenario 2.pdf ---
Unified University Inventory System (UUIS)
So basically right now we've got no single way of tracking 
everything the university owns across the faculties — 
computers, furniture, software licenses, rooms, even who's 
sitting where — and it's all over the place depending on which 
department you ask. Each faculty kind of does its own thing 
with spreadsheets or whatever old system they inherited, and 
nobody at the university level can just look something up and 
trust the answer. We want to build one system that everybody 
logs into, students, staff, IT people, deans, whoever, and 
depending on who they are they can see and manage the stuff 
that's relevant to them, but it's all sitting in one place 
instead of scattered everywhere. 
 
The way I picture it, once someone logs in (and for the people 
with more access we probably want something extra like a voice 
check, not just a password) they land on a menu where they can 
look up people, assets, locations and licenses, add new ones, 
edit them, get rid of stuff that's no longer around. Nothing 
should ever really disappear though, more like get marked as 
inactive so we keep history. People should also be able to 
lump assets or rooms into groups, like all the printers on a 
floor, or split things into subgroups, and bring in old data 
from CSV files from whatever system they're using today 
instead of typing everything from scratch. 
 
There's also this whole request and approval thing that 
matters a lot to us. If someone wants to move an item, report 
something broken, or just ask for a new asset, they should be 
able to submit that and it goes up to whoever's one level 
above them to approve or deny it, and if they say no they need 
to actually explain why. The exception is the people at the 
very top, university-level admins basically, their requests 
just go through automatically since there's nobody above to 
check them. Speaking of levels, this is kind of the backbone 
of the whole thing: department, faculty, university, and then 
a base user level, and what you can see and touch depends on 
where you sit, a faculty admin can reach into all the 
departments under them but a department admin only sees their 
own patch. 
 
We also want decent search, both a quick one where you just 
type something and a more detailed one where you can filter by 
different fields and combine conditions, plus some basic 
reporting, like comparing how many chairs or computers a room 
has against its supposed capacity. And everything anyone does 
in the system needs to get logged somewhere so if there's ever 
a question about who changed what, someone with the right 
permission can pull that up. 
 
A couple more things that matter even if they're not the 
flashy part. We can't have more than about two hundred people 
hammering the system at the same time, so it needs to hold up 
under that kind of load without falling over. If nobody 
touches it for half an hour, just log them out automatically, 
we don't want sessions sitting open forever. And if something 
crashes or a connection drops halfway through someone entering 
data, whatever they hadn't saved yet needs to come back to 
them when they log back in instead of just vanishing, losing 
someone's work because the system hiccuped would be a 
nightmare. On the security side, everything going over the 
network needs to be encrypted properly, and let's put a 
CAPTCHA on anything automated so bots can't just hammer the 
login. 
 
Things like managing permissions themselves, creating new 
roles, tweaking what each role can do, that's more of an 
admin-only corner of the system and honestly not the part 
we're most excited about, it just needs to exist so the 
higher-ups can keep control. Multiple languages and that kind 
of polish, plus the heavier department and faculty specific 
functions, those can wait for a later version, we're fine if 
version one is English-only and covers the main stuff for now. 
What we really care about for this first round is getting 
people, assets, locations and licenses all visible and 
manageable in one web system that anyone in the university can 
log into through a browser without needing anything special 
installed.

Sistema: Unified University Inventory System (UUIS)

Resumo executivo: The Unified University Inventory System centralizes university-wide information about people, assets, locations, workspace assignments, and software licenses. It replaces fragmented spreadsheets and legacy systems with a browser-based repository governed by hierarchical access controls, approval workflows, audit trails, search, reporting, and data-import capabilities.

Escopo: A centralized web system for managing university inventory information and related requests across departments and faculties.
  Em escopo: Authentication and role-based access
  Em escopo: Management of people, assets, locations, workspace assignments, and software licenses
  Em escopo: Hierarchical asset and location groups
  Em escopo: CSV data import
  Em escopo: Asset movement, damage-reporting, and acquisition requests
  Em escopo: Hierarchical request approval
  Em escopo: Quick and advanced search
  Em escopo: Room capacity comparison reports
  Em escopo: Audit logging and authorized audit consultation
  Em escopo: Administrative role and permission management
  Fora de escopo: Multiple-language support — deferred beyond version one
  Fora de escopo: Advanced department-specific and faculty-specific functions — deferred to a later version
  Fora de escopo: Native desktop or mobile applications — the first version is browser-based
  Fora de escopo: Direct integrations with legacy systems — only CSV import is specified
  Fora de escopo: Automated purchasing or supplier management — not described in the scenario
  Premissa: PA-01: Every user will have an active university identity before accessing the system. [INFERRED]
  Premissa: PA-02: Departments and faculties will designate administrators responsible for their inventory data. [INFERRED]
  Premissa: PA-03: Legacy data owners will provide CSV files conforming to an agreed import template. [INFERRED]
  Premissa: PA-04: Each department belongs to one faculty, and each faculty belongs to the university. [INFERRED]
  Premissa: PA-05: University network connectivity and supported web browsers will be available to users.
  Restrição: REST-01 (Platform): The first release must operate through a web browser without client-side installation.
  Restrição: REST-02 (Localization): The first release must provide an English-only user interface.
  Restrição: REST-03 (Capacity): The system must support approximately 200 concurrent users.
  Restrição: REST-04 (Security): Network communications must be encrypted.
  Restrição: REST-05 (Session): An inactive session must expire after 30 minutes.
  Restrição: REST-06 (Data retention): Retired records must be inactivated rather than physically deleted.
  Restrição: REST-07 (Scope): Advanced faculty-specific and department-specific functions are deferred.

Stakeholders:
  STK-01 - Student or Staff Member (Usuário primário): Search permitted inventory information, view relevant assignments, and submit movement, damage, or asset acquisition requests.
  STK-02 - Department Administrator (Usuário primário): Manage records and requests belonging to the administrator's department.
  STK-03 - Faculty Administrator (Usuário primário): Manage records and requests for every department within the administrator's faculty.
  STK-04 - University Administrator (Usuário primário): Manage university-wide inventory, approve or automatically process requests, and control roles and permissions.
  STK-05 - IT and Inventory Staff (Usuário primário): Maintain assets and licenses, import legacy data, process damage reports, and investigate inventory history.
  STK-06 - Dean and University Leadership (Usuário secundário): Access trusted consolidated inventory information and capacity reports for decision-making.
  STK-07 - Authorized Auditor (Usuário secundário): Retrieve immutable records identifying who performed each relevant system action. [INFERRED]

Regras de negócio:
  RN-001 - Hierarchical information scope: A base user may access only authorized information, a department administrator may access the administrator's department, a faculty administrator may access all departments within the administrator's faculty, and a university administrator may access the entire university.
  RN-002 - One-level approval: Movement, damage, and asset acquisition requests must be reviewed by an authorized person one organizational level above the requester.
  RN-003 - Mandatory denial justification: Every denied request must include a justification provided by the decision-maker.
  RN-004 - University-level automatic approval: Requests submitted by university administrators are automatically approved because no higher approval level exists.
  RN-005 - Non-destructive retirement: People, assets, locations, and licenses that are no longer current must be marked inactive while their historical information remains retained.
  RN-006 - Action accountability: Relevant actions must remain attributable to the person who performed them, including the action, affected record, date, and time.
  RN-007 - Administrative access control: Only authorized university-level administrators may create roles or change the permissions assigned to roles.
  RN-008 - Hierarchical grouping: Assets and locations may belong to groups, and groups may be divided into subordinate groups.
  RN-009 - Room capacity comparison: The recorded quantity of an asset category in a room may be compared with that room's registered capacity.
  RN-010 - Additional privileged-user verification: Users assigned privileged access must complete an additional identity-verification factor beyond a password. [INFERRED][TBD]

Requisitos funcionais:
  RF-001 - User authentication: The system shall authenticate an active user using registered credentials. [Must have]
  RF-002 - Privileged voice verification: The system shall require voice verification from users assigned privileged access. [TBD] [Should have]
  RF-003 - Access-sensitive menu: The system shall display menu functions according to the authenticated user's permissions. [Must have]
  RF-004 - Record consultation: The system shall allow authorized users to consult people, asset, location, workspace-assignment, and license records. [Must have]
  RF-005 - Record creation: The system shall allow authorized users to create people, asset, location, workspace-assignment, and license records. [Must have]
  RF-006 - Record editing: The system shall allow authorized users to edit people, asset, location, workspace-assignment, and license records. [Must have]
  RF-007 - Record inactivation: The system shall inactivate obsolete people, asset, location, workspace-assignment, and license records without physically deleting their history. [Must have]
  RF-008 - Workspace assignment: The system shall associate a person with an authorized room or workspace. [Must have]
  RF-009 - Group creation: The system shall allow authorized users to create groups containing assets or locations. [Should have]
  RF-010 - Subgroup creation: The system shall allow authorized users to create a subgroup beneath an existing asset or location group. [Should have]
  RF-011 - CSV import: The system shall import people, asset, location, and license records from a validated CSV file. [Must have]
  RF-012 - Movement request: The system shall allow an authorized user to submit a request to move an asset. [Must have]
  RF-013 - Damage report: The system shall allow an authorized user to submit a report identifying a damaged asset. [Must have]
  RF-014 - Asset acquisition request: The system shall allow an authorized user to submit a request for a new asset. [Must have]
  RF-015 - Approval routing: The system shall route a submitted request to an authorized approver one organizational level above the requester. [Must have]
  RF-016 - Request approval: The system shall allow the assigned approver to approve a pending request. [Must have]
  RF-017 - Request denial: The system shall require the assigned approver to provide a justification when denying a request. [Must have]
  RF-018 - Automatic top-level approval: The system shall automatically approve requests submitted by a university administrator. [Must have]
  RF-019 - Hierarchical access enforcement: The system shall restrict each operation and record to the authenticated user's authorized organizational scope. [Must have]
  RF-020 - Quick search: The system shall search authorized records using a single free-text query. [Must have]
  RF-021 - Advanced search: The system shall search authorized records using multiple field filters combined by logical conditions. [Should have]
  RF-022 - Room capacity report: The system shall generate a report comparing the recorded quantity of a selected asset category in each room against the room's registered capacity. [Should have]
  RF-023 - Audit event recording: The system shall record the actor, action, affected record, previous value, resulting value, date, and time for each data-changing operation. [Must have]
  RF-024 - Audit trail consultation: The system shall allow authorized users to retrieve audit events using actor, action, record, and date-range filters. [Must have]
  RF-025 - Role creation: The system shall allow a university administrator to create an access-control role. [Should have]
  RF-026 - Permission configuration: The system shall allow a university administrator to configure the permissions assigned to a role. [Should have]
  RF-027 - CAPTCHA validation: The system shall require successful CAPTCHA validation at login and other publicly accessible automated entry points. [TBD] [Must have]

Requisitos não funcionais:
  RNF-001 (Performance Efficiency) - The system shall support 200 concurrent active users with an HTTP error rate below 1%. | Métrica: 200 concurrent users; error rate below 1%; zero application crashes during a 60-minute load test.
  RNF-002 (Performance Efficiency) - The system shall complete 95% of interactive requests within 3 seconds under a load of 200 concurrent users. [TBD] | Métrica: 95th-percentile response time less than or equal to 3 seconds with 200 concurrent users. [TBD]
  RNF-003 (Security) - The system shall terminate an authenticated session after 30 consecutive minutes without user activity. | Métrica: 100% of tested sessions expire at 30 minutes, with a tolerance of plus or minus 5 seconds.
  RNF-004 (Reliability) - The system shall preserve recoverable form drafts at intervals no longer than 10 seconds and restore the most recent draft after an interrupted session. [TBD] | Métrica: 100% restoration of the latest draft saved no more than 10 seconds before a simulated connection or application failure. [TBD]
  RNF-005 (Security) - The system shall encrypt 100% of network communications using TLS 1.2 or later. [TBD] | Métrica: 100% of application endpoints use HTTPS; connections below TLS 1.2 are rejected. [TBD]
  RNF-006 (Compatibility) - The system shall complete all critical user journeys without critical errors on the two latest stable versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari. [TBD] | Métrica: Zero critical cross-browser defects across 100% of critical user journeys on the specified browser versions. [TBD]
  RNF-007 (Reliability) - The system shall maintain monthly availability of at least 99.5%, excluding scheduled maintenance. [TBD] | Métrica: At least 99.5% monthly availability and no more than 3.6 hours of unplanned downtime per month. [TBD]
  RNF-008 (Security) - The system shall retain 100% of audit records for at least seven years without allowing ordinary users to modify them. [TBD] | Métrica: 100% retention for seven years and zero successful unauthorized modification attempts. [TBD]
  RNF-009 (Security) - The system shall provide voice verification with a false-acceptance rate no greater than 0.1% and a false-rejection rate no greater than 5%. [TBD] | Métrica: False-acceptance rate less than or equal to 0.1%; false-rejection rate less than or equal to 5%. [TBD]

Casos de uso:
  UC-001 - Authenticate user | Ator: University user
    1. The actor opens the UUIS login page.
    2. The actor completes CAPTCHA validation and enters registered credentials.
    3. The system validates the credentials and account status.
    4. The system creates the session and displays the access-sensitive menu.
  UC-002 - Create inventory record | Ator: Department Administrator
    1. The actor selects a record type.
    2. The system displays the corresponding registration form.
    3. The actor enters the required data and submits the form.
    4. The system validates and saves the record.
    5. The system displays the generated record identifier.
  UC-003 - Inactivate inventory record | Ator: Department Administrator
    1. The actor opens an active record.
    2. The actor selects the inactivation operation.
    3. The system requests confirmation.
    4. The actor confirms the operation.
    5. The system changes the status to inactive and records the audit event.
  UC-004 - Create inventory subgroup | Ator: Inventory Staff Member
    1. The actor opens an existing group.
    2. The actor selects the subgroup creation function.
    3. The actor enters the subgroup details.
    4. The system validates and creates the subgroup.
  UC-005 - Import legacy CSV data | Ator: Inventory Staff Member
    1. The actor selects the record type and CSV file.
    2. The system validates the file structure and rows.
    3. The system displays a validation summary.
    4. The actor confirms the import.
    5. The system imports valid rows and displays totals.
  UC-006 - Submit asset movement request | Ator: Authorized University User
    1. The actor selects an asset and requests a movement.
    2. The actor specifies the proposed destination and reason.
    3. The system validates the request.
    4. The system determines the appropriate approval level.
    5. The system submits the request with the resulting status.
  UC-007 - Approve pending request | Ator: Assigned Approver
    1. The actor opens the assigned request.
    2. The system displays the request details.
    3. The actor selects approval.
    4. The system records the decision and changes the status to approved.
  UC-008 - Deny pending request | Ator: Assigned Approver
    1. The actor opens the pending request.
    2. The actor selects denial.
    3. The system requests a justification.
    4. The actor enters the justification and confirms.
    5. The system records the justification and changes the status to denied.
  UC-009 - Perform advanced search | Ator: Inventory Staff Member
    1. The actor opens advanced search.
    2. The actor selects fields, operators, values, and logical conditions.
    3. The system validates the search expression.
    4. The system displays matching records within the actor's scope.
  UC-010 - Generate room capacity report | Ator: Dean
    1. The actor selects a room scope and asset category.
    2. The system retrieves authorized rooms, capacities, and asset counts.
    3. The system calculates the difference between each count and capacity.
    4. The system displays the comparison report.
  UC-011 - Retrieve audit trail | Ator: Authorized Auditor
    1. The actor opens the audit trail.
    2. The actor provides one or more filters.
    3. The system retrieves matching events.
    4. The system displays the actor, action, record, values, date, and time.
  UC-012 - Configure role permissions | Ator: University Administrator
    1. The actor opens an access-control role.
    2. The system displays its current permissions.
    3. The actor changes the permission selections.
    4. The system requests confirmation.
    5. The actor confirms and the system saves the permission set.

Critérios de aceite:
  CA-001 - Dado an active user has valid registered credentials, quando the user submits the valid credentials, então the system creates an authenticated session and displays the authorized menu within 3 seconds [TBD]
  CA-002 - Dado a user with privileged access has passed password authentication, quando the user attempts to complete login, então the system requires successful voice verification before creating the privileged session
  CA-003 - Dado an authenticated user has a defined permission set, quando the main menu is displayed, então the menu displays 100% of permitted functions and zero functions explicitly prohibited for the role
  CA-004 - Dado an authenticated user has consultation permission, quando the user opens a people, asset, location, workspace-assignment, or license record, então the system displays the requested record if it belongs to the user's authorized scope
  CA-005 - Dado an authorized administrator has supplied all required valid fields, quando the administrator submits the creation form, então the system creates one active record with a unique identifier and displays 'Record created successfully'
  CA-006 - Dado an authorized administrator has opened an existing record, quando the administrator submits valid changed values, então the system persists the new values and displays 'Record updated successfully'
  CA-007 - Dado an authorized administrator has selected an active record, quando the administrator confirms inactivation, então the system changes the record status to 'Inactive' while retaining its historical values
  CA-008 - Dado an active person and authorized workspace exist, quando the administrator confirms the assignment, então the system stores the association and displays it in both the person's and workspace's details
  CA-009 - Dado an authorized inventory staff member has selected assets or locations, quando the staff member submits a valid group name, então the system creates the group with a unique identifier and the selected members
  CA-010 - Dado an authorized staff member has selected an existing parent group, quando the staff member submits valid subgroup details, então the system creates the subgroup directly beneath the parent without creating a circular relationship
  CA-011 - Dado an authorized staff member has uploaded a CSV file matching the agreed template, quando the staff member confirms the import, então the system imports 100% of valid rows and reports imported, rejected, and total row counts
  CA-012 - Dado an authorized user has selected an asset and valid destination, quando the user submits the movement request, então the system creates the request with status 'Pending approval' or 'Approved' for a university administrator
  CA-013 - Dado an authorized user has selected an active asset and entered a damage description, quando the user submits the report, então the system creates a uniquely identified damage request and assigns the applicable approval status
  CA-014 - Dado an authorized user has entered the required new-asset request details, quando the user submits the request, então the system creates a uniquely identified acquisition request and assigns the applicable approval status
  CA-015 - Dado a non-university-level user has submitted a valid request, quando the system determines the requester's organizational level, então the request is assigned to an authorized approver exactly one organizational level above the requester
  CA-016 - Dado an approver has an assigned request with status 'Pending approval', quando the approver confirms approval, então the system changes the status to 'Approved' and records the approver and decision timestamp
  CA-017 - Dado an approver has selected denial for a pending request, quando the approver attempts to confirm with a blank justification, então the system preserves status 'Pending approval' and displays 'Denial justification is required'
  CA-018 - Dado an authenticated university administrator has completed a valid request, quando the administrator submits the request, então the system assigns status 'Approved' without creating a pending approval task
  CA-019 - Dado an authenticated department administrator attempts to access another department's record, quando the access request is processed, então the system returns status 'Access denied', discloses no protected record data, and records the attempt
  CA-020 - Dado an authenticated user has entered a free-text query, quando the user submits the quick search, então the system displays only authorized records containing the query in configured searchable fields
  CA-021 - Dado an authorized user has defined two or more valid field conditions, quando the user executes the advanced search, então the system returns only authorized records satisfying the selected logical combination
  CA-022 - Dado authorized rooms have registered capacities and asset counts, quando the user generates a report for an asset category, então the report displays each room's capacity, asset count, and numeric difference
  CA-023 - Dado an authenticated user changes a managed record, quando the change is successfully committed, então the system records the actor, action, record identifier, previous value, resulting value, date, and time for 100% of changed fields
  CA-024 - Dado an authorized auditor has supplied valid actor, action, record, or date-range filters, quando the auditor executes the audit query, então the system displays all matching audit events without permitting their modification
  CA-025 - Dado an authenticated university administrator has entered a unique role name, quando the administrator confirms role creation, então the system creates the role and displays 'Role created successfully'
  CA-026 - Dado an authenticated university administrator has selected an existing role, quando the administrator confirms a changed permission set, então the system stores the new permission set and applies it to subsequent authorization checks
  CA-027 - Dado a login or exposed automated entry point requires CAPTCHA validation, quando the submitted CAPTCHA response is invalid, então the system rejects the operation and displays 'CAPTCHA validation failed'

Glossário:
  Asset: A physical item owned or controlled by the university, such as a computer, printer, or item of furniture.
  Base User: A student or staff member with access limited to explicitly authorized records and operations.
  Department: An organizational unit subordinate to a faculty.
  Faculty: An organizational unit containing one or more departments.
  University Administrator: A top-level administrator authorized to access university-wide information and administer roles and permissions.
  Location: A university-controlled physical place, including buildings, floors, rooms, or workspaces.
  Workspace Assignment: The recorded association between a person and a room, desk, seat, or other workspace.
  Software License: A recorded entitlement permitting use of a software product under specified terms.
  Group: A named collection of related assets or locations.
  Subgroup: A group positioned directly beneath another group in the inventory hierarchy.
  Request: A submitted proposal concerning asset movement, asset damage, or acquisition of a new asset.
  Approver: An authorized person one organizational level above a requester who may approve or deny the request.
  Inactive Record: A retained historical record excluded from current operations without physical deletion.
  Audit Event: An immutable record identifying an actor, action, affected data, previous and resulting values, date, and time.
  CSV: Comma-Separated Values, a tabular text format used to import legacy data.
  CAPTCHA: A challenge intended to distinguish human interaction from automated bot activity.
  Privileged Access: Access that permits administrative, university-wide, audit, role-management, or permission-management operations.

Base de Conhecimento em Engenharia
de Requisitos
Padrões, modelos e exemplos para elicitação e especificação de requisitos de software
conforme ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 · ISO/IEC 25010:2023 · SWEBOK v4.0 · BABOK® v3
Este documento é a base de conhecimento fixa (Vector Store B) do sistema de elicitação de requisitos. Ele ensina ao agente
de IA os padrões de escrita, templates, exemplos e regras de qualidade que devem ser aplicados ao analisar documentos 
de projeto.PARTE 1 — Estrutura do Documento de Especificação de Requisitos (SRS)
Base: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §9.6 · IEEE 830-1998 §3 · Sommerville (2016, cap. 4)
O Documento de Especificação de Requisitos de Software (SRS) é o contrato técnico que descreve o 
que o sistema deve fazer e sob quais condições de qualidade. Ele serve de referência para 
desenvolvedores, testadores, gerentes e clientes durante todo o ciclo de vida do projeto.
1.1 Artefatos Obrigatórios e sua Ordem
Um SRS completo e formal deve conter os seguintes artefatos, nesta ordem:
• ESCOPO: Define o que está DENTRO e FORA do projeto. Evita scope creep.
• STAKEHOLDERS: Lista todos os envolvidos: quem usa, quem financia, quem é afetado.
• PREMISSAS E RESTRIÇÕES: Fatos assumidos como verdadeiros e limites impostos ao projeto.
• REGRAS DE NEGÓCIO (RN): Políticas, fórmulas e condições de negócio que existem independentemente 
do software.
• REQUISITOS FUNCIONAIS (RF): O que o sistema DEVE FAZER — comportamentos, serviços, respostas a 
entradas.
• REQUISITOS NÃO FUNCIONAIS (RNF): Como o sistema deve SER — atributos de qualidade 
quantificáveis.
• HISTÓRIAS DE USUÁRIO (HU): Necessidades na perspectiva do usuário: Como [perfil], quero [ação], para
[benefício].
• CASOS DE USO (UC): Interações detalhadas ator-sistema com fluxo principal, alternativo e exceções.
• CRITÉRIOS DE ACEITE (CA): Condições testáveis em formato BDD (Dado/Quando/Então) que definem 
quando o requisito está concluído.
• GLOSSÁRIO: Termos do domínio com definição precisa para eliminar ambiguidades.
1.2 Como os Artefatos se Interconectam
Os artefatos formam uma cadeia de rastreabilidade. Cada RF deve ter origem em um STK 
(stakeholder) ou RN. Cada HU deve ter pelo menos um RF associado. Cada RF e HU devem ter pelo menos um CA. Esta rastreabilidade garante que nada seja implementado sem justificativa de 
negócio e que tudo que foi prometido seja testável.

So basically right now we've got no single way of tracking 
everything the university owns across the faculties — 
computers, furniture, software licenses, rooms, even who's 
sitting where — and it's all over the place depending on which 
department you ask. Each faculty kind of does its own thing 
with spreadsheets or whatever old system they inherited, and 
nobody at the university level can just look something up and 
trust the answer. We want to build one system that everybody 
logs into, students, staff, IT people, deans, whoever, and 
depending on who they are they can see and manage the stuff 
that's relevant to them, but it's all sitting in one place 
instead of scattered everywhere. 
The way I picture it, once someone logs in (and for the people 
with more access we probably want something extra like a voice 
check, not just a password) they land on a menu where they can 
look up people, assets, locations and licenses, add new ones, 
edit them, get rid of stuff that's no longer around. Nothing 
should ever really disappear though, more like get marked as 
inactive so we keep history. People should also be able to 
lump assets or rooms into groups, like all the printers on a 
floor, or split things into subgroups, and bring in old data 
from CSV files from whatever system they're using today 
instead of typing everything from scratch. 
There's also this whole request and approval thing that 
matters a lot to us. If someone wants to move an item, report 
something broken, or just ask for a new asset, they should be 
able to submit that and it goes up to whoever's one level 
above them to approve or deny it, and if they say no they need 
to actually explain why. The exception is the people at the 
very top, university-level admins basically, their requests 
just go through automatically since there's nobody above to 
check them. Speaking of levels, this is kind of the backbone 
of the whole thing: department, faculty, university, and then 
a base user level, and what you can see and touch depends on 
where you sit, a faculty admin can reach into all the 
departments under them but a department admin only sees their 
own patch. We also want decent search, both a quick one where you just 
type something and a more detailed one where you can filter by 
different fields and combine conditions, plus some basic 
reporting, like comparing how many chairs or computers a room 
has against its supposed capacity. And everything anyone does 
in the system needs to get logged somewhere so if there's ever 
a question about who changed what, someone with the right 
permission can pull that up. 
A couple more things that matter even if they're not the 
flashy part. We can't have more than about two hundred people 
hammering the system at the same time, so it needs to hold up 
under that kind of load without falling over. If nobody 
touches it for half an hour, just log them out automatically, 
we don't want sessions sitting open forever. And if something 
crashes or a connection drops halfway through someone entering 
data, whatever they hadn't saved yet needs to come back to 
them when they log back in instead of just vanishing, losing 
someone's work because the system hiccuped would be a

Expected challenges
The presence of an existing system leads to common challenges that both enhancement and 
replacement projects will face, including the following:
■ The changes made could degrade the performance to which users are accustomed.
■ Little or no requirements documentation might be available for the existing system.
■ Users who are familiar with how the system works today might not like the changes they are 
about to encounter.
■ You might unknowingly break or omit functionality that is vital to some stakeholder group.
■ Stakeholders might take this opportunity to request new functionality that seems like a good 
idea but isn’t really needed to meet the business objectives.
Even if there is existing documentation, it might not prove useful. For enhancement projects, 
the documentation might not be up to date. If the documentation doesn’t match the existing 
application’s reality, it is of limited use. For replacement systems, you also need to be wary of carrying 
forward all of the requirements, because some of the old functionality probably should not be 
migrated.
One of the major issues in replacement projects is validating that the reasons for the replacement 
are sound. There need to be justifiable business objectives for the change. When existing systems 
are being completely replaced, organizational processes might also have to change, which makes it 
harder for people to accept a new system. The change in business processes, change in the software 
system, and learning curve of a new system can disrupt current operations.

Which requirements should you specify?
It’s not always worth taking the time to generate a complete set of requirements for an entire 
production system. Many options lie between the two extremes of continuing forever with no 
requirements documentation and reconstructing a perfect requirements set. Knowing why you’d like 
to have written requirements available lets you judge whether the cost of rebuilding all—or even 
part—of the specification is a sound investment.

Level of detail
One of the biggest challenges is determining the appropriate level of detail at which to document 
requirements gleaned from the existing system. For enhancements, defining requirements for the 
new functionality alone might be sufficient. However, you will usually benefit from documenting all of 
the functionality that closely relates to the enhancement, to ensure that the change fits in seamlessly 
(region B in Figure 21-2). You might want to create business processes, user requirements, and/or 
functional requirements for those related areas. For example, let’s say you are adding a discount code 
feature to an existing shopping cart function, but you don’t have any documented requirements for 
the shopping cart. You might be tempted to write just a single user story: “As a customer, I need to be 
able to enter a discount code so I can get the cheapest price for the product.” However, this user story 
alone lacks context, so consider capturing other user stories about shopping cart operations. That 
information could be valuable the next time you need to modify the shopping cart function.
I worked with one team that was just beginning to develop the requirements for version 2 of 
a major product with embedded software. They hadn’t done a good job on the requirements for 
version 1, which was currently being implemented. The lead BA wondered, “Is it worth going back 
to improve the SRS for version 1?” The company anticipated that this product line would be a major 
revenue generator for at least 10 years. They also planned to reuse some of the core requirements 
in several spin-off products. In this case, it made sense to improve the requirements documentation 
for version 1 because it was the foundation for all subsequent development work in this product line.

3.2.4 Cenários e storyboards (L3)
Os cenários de uso descrevem, na forma de um exemplo realista, como um usuário 
interagirá com o sistema proposto [RoCa2002].
Um storyboard é um cenário visualizado. Ele se parece com uma história em quadrinhos, 
com um conjunto de imagens e/ou capturas de tela e, portanto, visualiza como um sistema 
ou produto deve ser usado. A reflexão sobre um exemplo concreto permite que clientes e 
usuários visualizem os requisitos na situação real do aplicativo e, assim, os revisem e alterem 
[RiFl2014].
3.3 Ferramentas de pensamento (L2)
As técnicas de elicitação apresentadas até agora representam técnicas que descrevem 
uma determinada maneira de coletar informações ou produzir um determinado produto de 
trabalho para fins de elicitação de requisitos.
Nesta seção, são apresentadas técnicas que cruzam esses tipos de técnicas, pois 
promovem uma determinada maneira de pensar. Nós as chamamos de técnicas de apoio e 
ferramentas de pensamento, porque elas não são aplicadas sozinhas, mas em conjunto com 
outras técnicas.
3.3.1 Pensamento em níveis de abstração (L2)
Os níveis de abstração são uma poderosa ferramenta de raciocínio na elicitação de 
requisitos [GoWo2005], [Laue2014]. Eles costumam ser usados como um tipo de modelo de 
processo para estruturar o trabalho de elicitação, ou seja, primeiro elicite os requisitos 
apenas no nível mais alto e continue com os níveis seguintes. Além disso, pode ser usado 
para estruturar as informações de requisitos obtidas, para identificar lacunas nos requisitos 
ou requisitos desnecessários e para concentrar as atividades de elicitação em um 
determinado nível de abstração. Por exemplo, em um workshop com usuários, é 
aconselhável concentrar-se no contexto do sistema, pois os usuários são os especialistas no 
contexto do sistema. Falar sobre as estruturas de dados de um sistema pode não ser 
apropriado, pois os usuários não se importam com as estruturas de dados internas.

3.7 Protótipos na Engenharia de Requisitos (L1)
Na ER, os protótipos são um meio de especificar os requisitos através do exemplo e de 
validar os requisitos. Em particular, os protótipos podem ser usados se os stakeholders não 
quiserem escrever e revisar produtos de trabalho baseados em linguagem natural ou em

Os protótipos exploratórios [LiSZ1994] são usados para criar um entendimento comum,

descartados após o uso.

CHAPTER 21
Enhancement and replacement 
projects
Most of this book describes requirements development as though you are beginning a new software 
or system development project, sometimes called a green-field project. However, many organizations 
devote much of their effort to enhancing or replacing existing information systems or building 
new releases of established commercial products. Most of the practices described in this book are 
appropriate for enhancement and replacement projects. This chapter provides specific suggestions as 
to which practices are most relevant and how to use them.
An enhancement project is one in which new capabilities are added to an existing system. 
Enhancement projects might also involve correcting defects, adding new reports, and modifying 
functionality to comply with revised business rules or needs.
A replacement (or reengineering) project replaces an existing application with a new custom-built 
system, a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) system, or a hybrid of those. Replacement projects are 
most commonly implemented to improve performance, cut costs (such as maintenance costs or 
license fees), take advantage of modern technologies, or meet regulatory requirements. If your 
replacement project will involve a COTS solution, the guidance presented in Chapter 22, “Packaged 
solution projects,” will also be helpful.
Replacement and enhancement projects face some particular requirements issues. The original 
developers who held all the critical information in their heads might be long gone. It’s tempting to 
claim that a small enhancement doesn’t warrant writing any requirements. Developers might believe 
that they don’t need detailed requirements if they are replacing an existing system’s functionality. 
The approaches described in this chapter can help you to deal with the challenges of enhancing or 
replacing an existing system to improve its ability to meet the organization’s current business needs.
The case of the missing spec
The requirements specification for the next release of a mature system often says, essentially, 
“The new system should do everything the old system does, except add these new features 
and fix those bugs.” A business analyst once received just such a specification for version 5 of 
a major product. To find out exactly what the current release did, she looked at the SRS for 
version 4. Unfortunately, it also said, in essence, “Version 4 should do everything that version 3 
does, except add these new features and fix those bugs.” She followed the trail back, but every

If developers build exactly what 
customers initially request, they’ll probably have to build it again because customers often don’t 
know what they really need. In addition, the BAs might not be talking to the right people or asking 
the right questions.
The features that users present as their “wants” don’t necessarily equate to the functionality they 
need to perform their tasks with the new product. To gain a more accurate view of user needs, the 
business analyst must collect a wide range of user input, analyze and clarify it, and specify just what 
needs to be built to let users do their jobs. The BA has the lead responsibility for recording the new 
system’s necessary capabilities and properties and for communicating that information to other 
stakeholders. This is an iterative process that takes time. If you don’t invest the time to achieve this 
shared understanding—this common vision of the intended product—the certain outcomes are 
rework, missed deadlines, cost overruns, and customer dissatisfaction.
User classes
People often talk about “the user” for a software system as though all users belong to a monolithic 
group with similar characteristics and needs. In reality, most products of any size appeal to a diversity 
of users with different expectations and goals. Rather than thinking of “the user” in singular, spend 
some time identifying the multiple user classes and their roles and privileges for your product.
Classifying users
Chapter 2 described many of the types of stakeholders that a project might have. As shown in 
Figure 6-1, a user class is a subset of the product’s users, which is a subset of the product’s customers, 
which is a subset of its stakeholders. An individual can belong to multiple user classes. For example, 
an application’s administrator might also interact with it as an ordinary user at times. A product’s 
users might differ—among other ways—in the following respects, and you can group users into a 
number of distinct user classes based on these sorts of differences:
■ Their access privilege or security levels (such as ordinary user, guest user, administrator)
■ The tasks they perform during their business operations
■ The features they use
■ The frequency with which they use the product
■ Their application domain experience and computer systems expertise
■ The platforms they will be using (desktop PCs, laptop PCs, tablets, smartphones, specialized 
devices)CHAPTER 6 Finding the voice of the user 103
■ Their native language
■ Whether they will interact with the system directly or indirectly
FIGURE 6-1 A hierarchy of stakeholders, customers, users, and user classes.
It’s tempting to group users into classes based on their geographical location or the kind of 
company they work in. One company that creates software used in the banking industry initially 
considered distinguishing users based on whether they worked in a large commercial bank, a small 
commercial bank, a savings and loan institution, or a credit union. These distinctions really represent 
different market segments, though, not different user classes.
A better way to identify user classes is to think about the tasks that various users will perform with 
the system. All of those types of financial institutions will have tellers, employees who process loan 
applications, business bankers, and so forth. The individuals who perform such activities—whether 
they are job titles or simply roles—will have similar functional needs for the system across all of the 
financial institutions. Tellers all have to do more or less the same things, business bankers do more or 
less the same things, and so on. More logical user class names for a banking system therefore might 
include teller, loan officer, business banker, and branch manager. You might discover additional user 
classes by thinking of possible use cases, user stories, and process flows and who might perform them.

Prioritizing by using business objectives
Enhancement projects are undertaken to add new capabilities to an existing application. It’s easy 
to get caught up in the excitement and start adding unnecessary capabilities. To combat this risk 
of gold-plating, trace requirements back to business objectives to ensure that the new features are 
needed and to select the highest-impact features to implement first. You also might need to prioritize 
enhancement requests against the correction of defects that had been reported against the old 
system.
Also be wary of letting unnecessary new functionality slip into replacement projects. The main 
focus of replacement projects is to migrate existing functionality. However, customers might imagine 
that if you are developing a new system anyway, it is easy to add lots of new capabilities right away. 
Many replacement projects have collapsed because of the weight of uncontrolled scope growth. 
You’re usually better off building a stable first release and adding more features through subsequent 
enhancement projects, provided the first release allows users to do their jobs.
Replacement projects often originate when stakeholders want to add functionality to an existing 
system that is too inflexible to support the growth or has technology limitations. However, there needs 
to be a clear business objective to justify implementing an expensive new system (Devine 2008). Use 
the anticipated cost savings from a new system (such as through reduced maintenance of an old, 
clunky system) plus the value of the new desired functionality to justify a system replacement project.
Also look for existing functionality that doesn’t need to be retained in a replacement system. Don’t 
replicate the existing system’s shortcomings or miss an opportunity to update a system to suit new 
business needs and processes. For example, the BA might ask users, “Do you use <a particular menu 
option>?” If you consistently hear “I never do that,” then maybe it isn’t needed in the replacement 
system. Look for usage data that shows what screens, functions, or data entities are rarely accessed 
in the current system. Even the existing functionality has to map to current and anticipated business 
objectives to warrant re-implementing it in the new system.
Trap Don’t let stakeholders get away with saying “I have it today, so I need it in the new 
system” as a default method of justifying requirements.
Mind the gap
A gap analysis is a comparison of functionality between an existing system and a desired new system. 
A gap analysis can be expressed in different ways, including use cases, user stories, or features. When 
enhancing an existing system, perform a gap analysis to make sure you understand why it isn’t 
currently meeting your business objectives.
Gap analysis for a replacement project entails understanding existing functionality and discovering 
the desired new functionality (see Figure 21-1). Identify user requirements for the existing system that 
stakeholders want to have re-implemented in the new system. Also, elicit new user requirements that 
the existing system does not address. Consider any change requests that were never implemented CHAPTER 21 Enhancement and replacement projects 397
in the existing system. Prioritize the existing user requirements and the new ones together. Prioritize 
closing the gaps using business objectives as described in the previous section or the other 
prioritization techniques presented in Chapter 16, “First things first: Setting requirement priorities.”
FIGURE 21-1 When you are replacing an existing system, some requirements will be implemented unchanged,

Maintaining performance levels
Existing systems set user expectations for performance and throughput. Stakeholders almost 
always have key performance indicators (KPIs) for existing processes that they will want to maintain 
in the new system.

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The user has an active registered identity.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The user has an authenticated session and sees the authorized menu.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor opens the UUIS login page.
2. The actor completes CAPTCHA validation and enters registered credentials.
3. The system validates the credentials and account status.
4. The system creates the session and displays the access-sensitive menu.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. The actor has privileged access → the system requests voice verification before continuing.
fluxos_excecao: 3b. The credentials are invalid or the account is inactive → the system displays 'Authentication failed' and does not create a session (RF-001).
2a. CAPTCHA validation fails → the system displays 'CAPTCHA validation failed' and rejects the attempt (RF-027).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The actor is authenticated and has creation permission for the selected organizational scope.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: A new active record exists within the actor's authorized scope.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor selects a record type.
2. The system displays the corresponding registration form.
3. The actor enters the required data and submits the form.
4. The system validates and saves the record.
5. The system displays the generated record identifier.
fluxos_alternativos: 1a. The actor selects a workspace assignment → the system requests the person and authorized workspace.
fluxos_excecao: 4a. Required data is missing or invalid → the system identifies each invalid field and does not create the record (RF-005).
4b. The selected scope is unauthorized → the system displays 'Access denied' and records the attempt (RN-001, RF-019).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The record is active and belongs to the actor's authorized scope.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The record has inactive status and remains available in history.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: The record remains active and unchanged.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor opens an active record.
2. The actor selects the inactivation operation.
3. The system requests confirmation.
4. The actor confirms the operation.
5. The system changes the status to inactive and records the audit event.
fluxos_alternativos: 4a. The actor cancels confirmation → the system returns to the unchanged record.
fluxos_excecao: 5a. The record is outside the actor's scope → the system displays 'Access denied' and preserves the record (RN-001, RF-019).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: A parent group exists within the actor's authorized scope.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The subgroup exists beneath the selected parent group.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor opens an existing group.
2. The actor selects the subgroup creation function.
3. The actor enters the subgroup details.
4. The system validates and creates the subgroup.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. The actor changes the selected parent → the system validates the new parent before submission.
fluxos_excecao: 4a. The relationship would create a cycle → the system displays 'Circular group relationships are not allowed' and rejects the operation (RN-008, RF-010).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The actor has import permission and possesses a CSV file.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: Valid rows are imported and an import summary is available.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: No invalid row is committed as a valid record.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor selects the record type and CSV file.
2. The system validates the file structure and rows.
3. The system displays a validation summary.
4. The actor confirms the import.
5. The system imports valid rows and displays totals.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. Some rows are invalid → the system identifies each invalid row and allows the actor to import only valid rows.
fluxos_excecao: 2a. The file structure is unsupported → the system displays 'Invalid CSV structure' and imports zero rows (RF-011).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The actor is authenticated and may view the asset.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The request is pending with the appropriate approver or automatically approved.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor selects an asset and requests a movement.
2. The actor specifies the proposed destination and reason.
3. The system validates the request.
4. The system determines the appropriate approval level.
5. The system submits the request with the resulting status.
fluxos_alternativos: 4a. The requester is a university administrator → the system automatically approves the request.
fluxos_excecao: 3a. The asset or destination is unauthorized → the system displays 'Asset or destination is outside your authorized scope' (RN-001, RF-019).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: A pending request is assigned to the actor.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The request has approved status and the decision is audited.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor opens the assigned request.
2. The system displays the request details.
3. The actor selects approval.
4. The system records the decision and changes the status to approved.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. The actor chooses denial → the denial flow is initiated.
fluxos_excecao: 4a. The request is no longer pending → the system displays 'Request has already been processed' and records no new decision (RF-016).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: A pending request is assigned to the actor.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The request has denied status with a stored justification.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor opens the pending request.
2. The actor selects denial.
3. The system requests a justification.
4. The actor enters the justification and confirms.
5. The system records the justification and changes the status to denied.
fluxos_alternativos: 4a. The actor cancels the denial → the request remains pending.
fluxos_excecao: 4b. The justification is blank → the system displays 'Denial justification is required' and does not deny the request (RN-003, RF-017).

fluxo_principal: 1. The actor opens advanced search.
2. The actor selects fields, operators, values, and logical conditions.
3. The system validates the search expression.
4. The system displays matching records within the actor's scope.
fluxos_alternativos: 4a. No record matches → the system displays 'No matching records found'.
fluxos_excecao: 3a. The expression is incomplete → the system identifies the invalid condition and does not execute the search (RF-021).

casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: A capacity comparison report is displayed.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: No misleading capacity comparison is produced.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor selects a room scope and asset category.
2. The system retrieves authorized rooms, capacities, and asset counts.
3. The system calculates the difference between each count and capacity.
4. The system displays the comparison report.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. A room has no capacity value → the system marks the room as 'Capacity data unavailable'.
fluxos_excecao: 2a. No room is available in the selected scope → the system displays 'No rooms available for this report' (RN-009, RF-022).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The actor is authenticated and has audit consultation permission.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: Matching audit events are displayed without modification.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: Audit data remains undisclosed and unchanged.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor opens the audit trail.
2. The actor provides one or more filters.
3. The system retrieves matching events.
4. The system displays the actor, action, record, values, date, and time.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. No event matches → the system displays 'No audit events found'.
fluxos_excecao: 1a. The actor lacks audit permission → the system displays 'Access denied' and records the attempt (RN-006, RF-024).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The actor is authenticated as a university administrator and the role exists.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The selected role contains the confirmed permission set.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: The previous permission set remains active.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor opens an access-control role.
2. The system displays its current permissions.
3. The actor changes the permission selections.
4. The system requests confirmation.
5. The actor confirms and the system saves the permission set.
fluxos_alternativos: 4a. The actor cancels confirmation → the previous permission set remains active.
fluxos_excecao: 5a. The actor lacks university-administrator authority → the system displays 'Access denied' and rejects the changes (RN-007, RF-026).

stakeholders.descricao: Base user (students, staff) — logs in with a password, access restricted to what is relevant to them.
Department admin — sees and manages only their own department's data; approves requests from base users below them.
Faculty admin — sees and manages all departments under their faculty; login requires an extra verification step (voice check).
University-level admin — top of the hierarchy; their requests are approved automatically, since there is no approver above them; manages permissions and roles.

regras_de_negocio.descricao: Higher-access users (department, faculty, and university admins) require an extra verification step (voice check) at login, in addition to a password.
Deleted records are never physically removed — only marked as inactive, to preserve history.
Requests to move an item, report something broken, or request a new asset go to the approver exactly one level above the requester.
Rejected requests require an explanation from the approver.
Requests from university-level admins are automatically approved, since there is no approver above them.
A faculty admin can access all departments in their faculty; a department admin only sees their own department.
Permission and role management is an admin-only feature.

historias_de_usuario.descricao: As a base user (student/staff), I want to log in and see only what's relevant to me, so that I can manage my own view of the inventory without irrelevant data.
As a higher-access user, I want to complete an extra verification step (voice check) at login, so that my elevated access is protected beyond just a password.
As a user, I want to look up, add, and edit people, assets, locations, and licenses, so that the inventory stays up to date.
As a user, I want to submit a request to move an item, report something broken, or request a new asset, so that the right approver can review it.
As an approver, I want to approve or reject requests from users one level below me, explaining any rejection, so that the requester understands the decision.
As a department admin, I want to see and manage only my own department's data, so that I don't interfere with other departments.
As a faculty admin, I want to see and manage all departments in my faculty, so that I have full oversight of it.
As a user, I want to search using quick search or advanced/filtered search, so that I can find records efficiently.
As a user with reporting access, I want to compare a room's capacity against its actual chairs/computers, so that I can identify discrepancies.
As an admin, I want to manage permissions and roles, so that I can control what each role is allowed to access.

casos_de_uso.descricao: Submit and approve request — a user submits a request (move item/report broken/new asset), the system routes it to the approver one level above, who approves or rejects it with an explanation (or it is auto-approved if the requester is a university-level admin).
Search inventory — a user performs a quick or advanced/filtered search across people, assets, locations, and licenses.
Import legacy data — an admin imports historical inventory data from a CSV file.
Generate room capacity report — a user runs a report comparing a room's stated capacity against its actual chairs/computers.
Manage roles and permissions — an admin creates or edits roles and adjusts what each role can access.

criterios_de_aceite.descricao: Given a higher-access user attempting to log in, when they enter their password, then the system requires an additional voice verification before granting access.
Given a user submits a request, when it is sent, then the system routes it to the approver exactly one level above the requester.
Given a university-level admin submits a request, when it is sent, then the system approves it automatically, without requiring further approval.
Given 200 concurrent users accessing the system, when they perform normal operations, then the system remains responsive without failing.
Given a user session with no activity, when 30 minutes pass, then the system automatically ends the session.
